Got cut off 1 by 1 from self inflected management commentary.

3. Then there was no M&A announcements, and that also turned into "looking at opportunities". 
4. Lot of long-term CPO economic opportunities were redirected into near term pluggable discussions. 

I'm not sure if it's a communication or cultural issue, but the underlying business got stronger. The ambitions they initially set with press releases in H1 were cut off. 

But valuation premiums can always come back depending on communication and subsequent execution next earnings.

text:
In terms of laser industry dynamics: 

- $LITE: "Take or pay. There's a very strong commitment from the customer side, and in some cases, there's a prepay element as well". Hyperscalers were explicitly funding their capacity expansion as well

- $COHR: Upfront payments in almost every LTA, according to its CEO. 

Both Lumentum and Coherent are the gold standard in terms of financing + demand signals. 

- For Chinese laser suppliers:

Optical module makers are actively financing their supply chains (even for lower range pluggables), as seen with Cambridge. 

In terms of US supply chains: 

- $AAOI CFO gave a note: "Customer financing is more likely for emerging technologies such as CPO and NPO than conventional 800G and 1.6T transceivers."

- $AAOI got a CPO + laser contract worth $700m for 2028-2029. But resulted in more ATMs instead of funding expansion with prepayments... 

I think people can agree AOI as a business at $3.7B MC is very operationally compelling:

- since they signed a $1B-$1.5B LTA with one hyperscaler
-  $2.2B LTA all in a single quarter.

But with management repeatedly creates expectations that later disclosures contrast with, which I agree is strange. 

Lot of current financing (as seen with Neoclouds) are done with prepayments given tightening. Or if a supplier is important enough (as seen with $SPCX), they'll help refinance the company. 

So I'm really not sure what's happening with $AAOI, maybe it's overstated competitive positioning or something else.

text:
$NUAI - the main catalysts I’m watching following the latest earnings call:

1. Phase 1 tenant agreement. 
Negotiations are at an advanced stage. Management said the economics were agreed, with technical details still being finalised. A signed lease is the biggest near-term catalyst. (I'm expecting a deal similar to the one secured by $RIOT with $ANT).

2. Phase 2 air permit. 
The application has been filed, and management expected approval before the end of 2026. 

3. Phase 2 tenant agreement.

text:
I spent a little bit of time reading Lab researcher / Hyperscaler expert calls on Tegus and building an ANT model (+AI GW Model)

My conclusion is that 2027 is going to get pretty crazy.

I don’t think I wrapped my head around just how much $ANT is going to be spending on training.

Market rightfully reacted when learning how little ANT was spending on serving customers vs. training with their ~25% split. The implication when you roll fwd Compute / % mix to training is pretty eye opening.

My ANT base case is they spend ~6x more on training/RL models by end of ‘27 vs. the current / Opus 5.5 class model. When you factor in efficiency gains (esp on the RL side), it is probably closer to a 10x increase in effective training. I personally can’t fathom what that leads to.

A huge amount of the debate will come down to:
What does it mean for ANT (and not too too far behind OAI) to spend 10x more effective compute training models over the next year?

There’s a camp that believes meaningful chunks of intelligence tap out – that for something like Coding, everyone will plateau at a similar point and with not too much training / RL bc the models essentially know how to solve this problem..RSI helps you get to the plateau faster bc the models know how to solve that problem (argument from META researcher below).

I’m more bullish on the frontier and have extreme excitement about what 10x more effective compute to train models by the end of ‘27 could mean: my read of the researcher expert

La somme des news qu'on a est juste délirante

Let me explain :

1. Comme un air de fin du monde

Il y a deux jours, Washington propose des tarifs de 20 à 35 % sur 14 partenaires, et le core PCE sort à 3,3 % contre 3,2 % attendu, la gifle est pénible. Le Nasdaq refait encore une de ses pires séances en 10 ans, il touche brièvement -20 % sous son record en rentrant en « Bear Market », et le VIX monte à près de 35

Et puis tout se retourne de façon un peu ridicule. À la clôture, tout est à l'équilibre. Le déclencheur le plus cité, c'est le feu vert de la FCC aux data centers orbitaux (ce qui est un peu risible). Côté marrant, Michael Burry aurait aussi fermé ses paris à la baisse sur le Nasdaq et Jim Cramer est passé short (lol)

Perso, j'y vois surtout des rachats de shorts dans des volumes faibles avant Thanksgiving et des équilibrages d'ETF à levier

The Fed and the Wall Street hawks calling for more hikes are steering by the rear-view mirror. Look forward and you can see it coming: ships returning to the Suez Canal, oil sliding into surplus, and a container fleet about to swell. 

That is a disinflationary supply shock, and the people setting policy are blind to it.

Start with the canal. The Suez Canal Authority reported 1,490 transits in October and $ 724 million of revenue, the strongest month since the Red Sea crisis began and nearly double a year earlier. 

Container traffic, as charted by Javier Blas at Bloomberg Opinion, has climbed from 20,000 TEU a day through most of 2024 and 2025 to 136,000. Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd restore all their Asia-Europe loops to Suez from 4 December.

The Cape detour added two to three weeks a voyage and absorbed 5 to 7 per cent of global container capacity. That capacity is coming back just as the fleet grows 9 per cent in 2027 and the orderbook sits at 45 per cent of existing ships. 

Shanghai to Rotterdam freight is already down 29 per cent from its July peak.

Then add energy. The IEA has the oil market in surplus now and a larger surplus in 2027, with supply up 6.6 million barrels a day. North Sea crude has fallen from $ 136 a barrel in October to about $ 93.

None of this shows up in a New Keynesian model, where growth is inflationary and every strong number demands another hike. The Fed has it backw

The bears say there is no AI demand in 2027 or 2028. False. Look at the data.

Memory: Goldman has DRAM short 4.1 per cent in 2026, 5.1 per cent in 2027 and 1.2 per cent in 2028. The 2027 gap is the widest in 15+ years. Demand beats supply every year.

Suppliers: Samsung’s 2027 HBM is sold out. SK hynix sees demand above supply through 2030. Micron has “no line of sight” to balance. New fabs arrive in 2028 and later.

Wafers: HBM rises to nearly 30 per cent of DRAM wafer input in 2027 and takes 3 to 4x the wafers per bit. 

Conventional DRAM gets squeezed.
CPUs: NVDA says agentic AI demand for CPUs is “far outstripping supply” and sees CPU revenue more than doubling.

GPUs: a three-year-old H100 rents for $ 3.07 an hour, up 54 per cent in a year. CoreWeave has 10x more demand than capacity through 2027, and 2028 is already several times capacity.

Capex: cloud spending is up another 60 per cent in 2027, to about $ 1.5 trillion.

If demand were fading, old chips would get cheaper. They are getting dearer.

AI demand is strong. Ignore the doomers.

The memory upcycle in two charts:

DRAM:
• Contract prices started climbing in 3Q25 and were up ~45% QoQ by 4Q25
• 1Q26 was the peak: blended ASP roughly doubled in one quarter, with PC DDR5 up ~110%
• 2Q26 added another ~60%, led by server DDR4 at ~70%

NAND:
• Later and a bit smaller: ~+30% in 4Q25, ~+57% in 1Q26, ~+75% in 2Q26
• Enterprise SSD led both quarters at ~+80%

What's forecast next:
• 3Q26: DRAM ~+15%, NAND ~+20%
• 4Q26: both around +10%
• 2027: DRAM flattens to low single digits, while NAND turns negative from 2Q27 and is falling 10–15% QoQ by 4Q27

Prices are still rising, but the rate of change peaked in 1H26. And the forecasts say NAND rolls over well before DRAM does.

text:
On Tuesday morning, I discussed with @YvonneManTV how the Chinese markets had reached an important low for the year, and the major Chinese indices had fallen to a level that suggested a strong rebound. 

Apparently, today’s press release from the State Council meeting contains some very unusual wording. 

Today’s State Council Executive Meeting (国常会) marks the first time the "National Team" (国家队) and Central Huijin’s quasi-stabilization fund (类“平准基金”) role appeared in a State Council readout. 

The wording “stabilization fund” was previously used only by Huijin (in April 2025) and financial regulators. Including it in the press release effectively institutionalized the Central Huijin’s role as a state stabilization fund. And it's significantly positive news for the market. 
$YINN $YANG $FXI $KWEB $CQQQ $EWH $PGJ $BABA $PDD
